title: Web Crawler
summary: Fetch and store billions of web pages politely for a search index.
statement:
Design a crawler that discovers and downloads web pages to feed a search index.

Functional requirements:
- Start from a seed list and follow links to discover new pages.
- Re-crawl pages periodically, more often for pages that change often.
- Respect robots rules and do not overload any single website.
- Store raw page content for downstream indexing.

Scale to assume:
- 5 billion pages fetched per month.
- Average page size of 100 KB.
- Many pages are duplicates or near-duplicates of one another.
hints: The list of URLs to fetch next is the heart of the system. How would you prioritize it and keep it polite per host?
How do you know you have already seen a URL, or a page with the same content, at this scale?
List what can go wrong when following links on the open web and how you would protect the crawler.
expectations: Clarifies freshness goals, content types, politeness rules, and what downstream indexing needs.
Estimates fetch rate (thousands of pages per second), bandwidth, and storage per month.
Designs a URL frontier with priority queues and per-host queues that enforce politeness delays.
Deduplicates URLs (normalized URL set or Bloom filter) and content (checksums or similarity hashes).
Caches robots rules and DNS lookups per host and distributes hosts across workers by consistent hashing.
Stores raw pages in object or blob storage with metadata in a separate store.
Guards against crawler traps, infinite URL spaces, malformed pages, and slow servers with timeouts and depth limits.
